title: Dhanaraj murder: Kannur court calls RSS convicts 'quockerwodgers', says police driven by CPM leader’s statement
content: Kannur: The three RSS men convicted of murdering CPM branch secretary C V Dhanaraj (38) were, in the words of the trial judge, quockerwodgers, political puppets who are controlled by someone else and act on their instructions. The word was recently popularised by Congress MP Shashi Tharoor, who in an X post, called it the 'word of our era', adding that the ruling BJP had spawned a few of these in the last dozen years. But in the Dhanaraj murder case, who was pulling the strings? Taliparamba Additional District and Sessions Judge, Prasanth K N, found that Dhanaraj's killing in 2016, which pushed Payyannur to the brink, was a "preplanned political murder". But he said the police were driven by the statement of CPM branch secretary P P Prajeesh and that their failure to resist Prajeesh's 'obstinacy' in trying to implicate certain persons led to the acquittal of some accused. Prajeesh was the prosecution's first witness, and the judge devoted 17 paragraphs to explaining why his testimony could not be relied upon. Even the special public prosecutor, Adv C K Sreedharan was frustrated with Prajeesh. He is a CPM branch secretary and a childhood friend of Dhanaraj. Dhanaraj was hacked 37 times in his compound around 9.45 pm, and he died around 11 pm at Pariyaram medical college. The witness left the hospital around 1 am, and his statement was recorded by Payyannur police around 2 am. But he told the court that in the four hours, he did not inform any party leaders about the attack on his comrade. "For the court, given that he was a party office-bearer, it was difficult to believe that he had not informed anyone about the incident before approaching the police, Adv Sreedharan told Onmanorama. The additional sessions court acquitted 16 of the 19 accused. Defence counsel P Premarajan said the police, under the newly formed LDF government, indiscriminately named RSS workers and mid-level leaders as accused in the case. Consecutive sentences The first three accused, T P Biju (34), Vipin M (34) and his younger brother Vaishakh M (31), were sentenced to life imprisonment for murdering Dhanaraj in front of his mother and wife at Karanthad in Ramanthali on July 11, 2016. They were also convicted under other IPC sections for trespass, causing hurt, wrongful restraint and criminal intimidation, for which they were sentenced to five years and four months. The conspiracy theory was discarded in the absence of credible evidence, no doubt in mind that it is a case of preplanned political murder, and the accused were used as the quockerwodgers, the judge wrote. Though the judge considered their young age (in their early 20s) to decide against the death penalty, he declined to show leniency in the sentences, ordering them to serve five years and four months of fixed-term imprisonment before their life terms begin. Each convict was also fined 5 lakh. The total amount of 15 lakh, if realised, will be paid to Dhanaraj's mother, C V Madhavi, and wife, N V Sajina, the judge ruled. If they fail to pay the fine, each will have to undergo an additional five years of rigorous imprisonment. The judge, however, observed that the convicts could not be expected to pay the fine given their poor financial background and directed the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA), Thalassery, to consider awarding compensation to the family under Section 357A(3) of the CrPC. Why the court accepted the identification The defence is planning to challenge the conviction of the three BJP-RSS workers, arguing that Dhanaraj's mother and wife were shown photographs of the accused before the test identification parade (TIP). But the Taliparamba Sessions Court addressed this objection in its judgment. The judge acknowledged that Dhanaraj's wife Sajini had told a magistrate that she had seen photographs of the accused on a mobile phone shown by her sister-in-law. However, the court held that this alone did not invalidate her identification...
